extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry/anabelian geometry (readers of Mochizuki's IUT papers)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and records the paper's notations, terminological conventions, and structural/algorithmic statements about categories, fundamental groups, and coverings used throughout the IUT I series. Intended to guide correct reading and reproduction of arguments in the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topological pseudo-monoid
rubrics_metrics.description: A topological space P with a continuous map P × P ⊇ S → P is a topological pseudo-monoid if there exists a topological abelian group M and an embedding ι : P → M such that S = {(a,b) in P×P | ι(a)·ι(b) ∈ ι(P)} and the map S→P is the restriction of M×M→M via ι. If M has discrete topology, call P a pseudo-monoid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every topological pseudo-monoid determines an underlying pseudo-monoid. This is the paper's chosen notion for working with partial/multiplicative structures embedded in groups; use ι and M to test properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisible pseudo-monoid
rubrics_metrics.description: A pseudo-monoid P is divisible if M and ι may be chosen so that for each positive integer n every element of M admits an n-th root in M, and an element a ∈ M lies in ι(P) iff a^n ∈ ι(P).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisibility is a structural hypothesis one can impose on a pseudo-monoid via the ambient group M; used when nth-root closure properties are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotomic pseudo-monoid
rubrics_metrics.description: P is cyclotomic if M and ι may be taken such that the torsion subgroup μ_M of M is isomorphic to Q/Z, μ_M ⊆ ι(P), and μ_M · ι(P) ⊆ ι(P).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This captures the presence of full cyclotomic torsion inside the embedded image; applies when exploiting torsion/cyclotomic symmetries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology: 'isomorph' of an object
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper refers to an isomorphic copy of some object simply as an 'isomorph' of the object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be alert: the author uses 'isomorph' as shorthand for 'an isomorphic copy' in many constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology: 'isomorphism C → D' for categories
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'isomorphism C → D' denotes any isomorphism class of equivalences of categories C → D (this differs from the standard category-theory phrasing but is natural in the paper's coarsification context).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the text says 'isomorphism' between categories, interpret it as an equivalence class of equivalences rather than a strict equality; this affects how one reads reconstruction/isomorphism statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poly-morphism / poly-isomorphism / poly-automorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: A poly-morphism A → B is a collection (subset) of morphisms A → B. If all morphisms are isomorphisms it's a poly-isomorphism; if A = B it's a poly-automorphism. Composition of poly-morphisms is defined by composing all pairs and ignoring multiplicities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formalism is used to handle collections of parallel maps (and multiplicities are ignored). Recognize poly- notions when reading constructions that assemble many morphisms simultaneously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capsule of objects and Capsule(C)
rubrics_metrics.description: A capsule of objects of a category C is a finite collection {A_j}_{j∈J}. A morphism of capsules {A_j}_{j∈J} → {A'_i}_{i∈I} consists of an injection ι: J→I plus, for each j, a morphism A_j → A'_{ι(j)}. Capsules form a category Capsule(C). A capsule-full poly-morphism is a poly-morphism associated to a fixed injection whose entries are collections of isomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to organize finite collections of objects and their interrelations; expect proofs that manipulate finite 'tuples' of objects to use this vocabulary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation B(X) and B(A)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a connected noetherian algebraic stack X (generically scheme-like), B(X) denotes the category of finite étale coverings of X (and morphisms over X); for a noetherian ring A, B(A) := B(Spec(A)). The connected subcategory is B(X)^0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the paper's standard notation for the finite-étale covering category; used when reconstructing fundamental groups or temperoid categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Btemp(Π), tempered groups, connected temperoid, and reconstruction of π1
rubrics_metrics.description: Btemp(Π) is the category of countable discrete sets with continuous Π-action. Π is 'tempered' if it is an inverse limit of surjections of countable discrete groups. A category equivalent to Btemp(Π) (with Π tempered) is a connected temperoid. If Π is Galois-countable then Π may be reconstructed category-theoretically from Btemp(Π) (or its connected subcategory), yielding π1(C) up to inner automorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the author speaks of reconstructing topological groups from categories of actions, this is the precise framework; it justifies passing between categorical data and π1-type groups throughout the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms between temperoids
rubrics_metrics.description: If C1, C2 are connected temperoids, a morphism C1 → C2 is an isomorphism class of functors C2 → C1 that preserves finite limits and countable colimits (a slight variant of [SemiAnbd] Def. 3.1(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret 'morphism' of temperoids as contravariant-type functors with the stated preservation properties; this affects how maps between fundamental-group-like categories are described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bijective correspondence: outer homomorphisms ↔ morphisms of Btemp
rubrics_metrics.description: For Galois-countable tempered groups Π1, Π2 there is a natural bijection between (a) continuous outer homomorphisms Π1 → Π2, (b) morphisms Btemp(Π1) → Btemp(Π2), and (c) morphisms Btemp(Π1)^0 → Btemp(Π2)^0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the explicit categorical ↔ group-theoretic dictionary used in many reconstruction arguments; use it to translate categorical maps into outer homomorphisms and vice versa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract equivalence of functors between categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Two isomorphism classes of functors φ : C1 → C2 and φ' : C1' → C2' are 'abstractly equivalent' if there exist isomorphisms α_i : C_i → C_i' such that φ' ◦ α1 = α2 ◦ φ. The terminology applies to temperoids and subcategories of connected objects as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the text equates functors up to conjugation by isomorphisms of source/target categories, interpret that as abstract equivalence in this sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations NF / MLF / CAF
rubrics_metrics.description: NF = number field, MLF = mixed-characteristic (nonarchimedean) local field, CAF = complex archimedean field, as in [AbsTopI], §0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These abbreviations are used throughout IUT I; recognize them when hypotheses reference base fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuation and completion notation V(F), F_v, integrality and p_v
rubrics_metrics.description: For a number field F, V(F) denotes the set of valuations (archimedean V(F)^arc and nonarchimedean V(F)^non). For v ∈ V(F), F_v is the completion; an element is integral at v if its v-norm ≤ 1. For possibly infinite Galois extension L of F, L_v denotes completion at some valuation over v. If v ∈ V(F)^non write p_v for the residue characteristic; if v ∈ V(F)^arc write p_v ∈ F_v for the unique positive real whose natural log is 1 (i.e., e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these conventions when reading statements about local/global behavior and integrality at places.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology for curves: hyperbolic curve, cusp, stable/smooth log curve, hyperbolic orbicurve
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper uses hyperbolic curve, cusp, stable log curve, smooth log curve as defined in [SemiAnbd], §0, and hyperbolic orbicurve as in [Cusp], §0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the paper refers to these curve types, interpret them according to the cited foundational sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption (*) in §1 constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: The standing assumption (*) used in §1: the natural action of G_k on Δ_X^{ab} ⊗ (Z/lZ) is trivial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many constructions and identifications in §1 rely on this triviality; verify assumption (*) when applying the §1 results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decomposition under involution ι and eigenspace splitting
rubrics_metrics.description: For the involution ι ∈ Gal(X/C) (the nontrivial element), its action on Δ (the relevant quotient) determines a decomposition Δ ≅ Δ^+ × Δ^− where ι acts by +1 on Δ^+ and by −1 on Δ^−; inertia images map isomorphically into the + eigenspace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this splitting when analyzing Galois actions and building quotients/sections that separate ±-eigenspaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 1.1: orbicurves of type (1, l-tors−−→) and (1, l-tors−−→)±
rubrics_metrics.description: A hyperbolic orbicurve over k that arises (up to isomorphism) as the hyperbolic orbicurve X^→ (resp. C^→) constructed for some choice of l and a cusp q is said to be of type (1, l-tors−−→) (resp. (1, l-tors−−→)±). The arrow denotes the ordered labels determined by the choice of cusp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This naming convention records the auxiliary choices (labels) used in the covering constructions; treat the arrowed notation as encoding that data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic Nature of Coverings (Corollary 1.2): algorithmic reconstruction
rubrics_metrics.description: If k is an NF or an MLF, there exists a functorial group-theoretic algorithm to reconstruct Π_X, Π_{C^→}, Π_C (resp. Π_{C}) together with the conjugacy classes of decomposition groups determined by the relevant cusps from Π_{X^→} (resp. Π_{C^→}). The reconstruction is functorial with respect to isomorphisms of topological groups, realizing the groups as subgroups of Aut(Π_{X^→}) (resp. Aut(Π_{C^→})).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement includes a proof sketch: use slimness to embed into automorphism groups, recover Δ-subgroups via [AbsTopI] algorithms, compute l from subgroup indices, set H = Ker(Δ_X → Δ_X^{ab}⊗(Z/lZ)) and recover Π_X as Π_{X^→}·H, reconstruct splittings by group-theoretic characterization, and identify decomposition conjugacy classes via images in finite quotients. Apply referenced algorithms/results ([AbsTopI], [AbsTopII], [EtTh]) in this order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functoriality and uniqueness of certain splittings
rubrics_metrics.description: In reconstructing Π_C ⊆ Π_C one recovers the splitting of Gal(X/C) = Π_C/Π_X inside Π_C by characterizing it group-theoretically as the unique splitting that stabilizes the collection of conjugacy classes of decomposition groups of the cusps. Similarly, Π_{C^→} is recovered because Z/2lZ is the unique maximal subgroup of odd index in the relevant quotient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reconstructing coverings and deck groups, employ the rigidity/uniqueness characterizations given (stabilizers of conjugacy classes, maximal subgroup of odd index) to pick the canonical splitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automorphism groups of the constructed covers (Remark 1.2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: As a consequence of Corollary 1.2, Aut_k(X^→) = Gal(X^→/C) ≅ Z/2lZ and Aut_k(C^→) = Gal(C^→/C) ≅ Z/lZ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record these concrete automorphism group identifications when using or citing the specific covers X^→, C^→ constructed in §1.
